title: The Goods and the Ills
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: There was a time in the youth of the world when Goods and Ills entered equally into the concerns of men, so that the Goods did not prevail to make them altogether blessed, nor the Ills to make them wholly miserable. But owing to the foolishness of mankind the Ills multiplied greatly in number and increased in strength, until it seemed as though they would deprive the Goods of all share in human affairs, and banish them from the earth.

The latter, therefore, betook themselves to heaven and complained to Jupiter of the treatment they had received, at the same time praying him to grant them protection from the Ills, and to advise them concerning the manner of their intercourse with men. Jupiter granted their request for protection, and decreed that for the future they should not go among men openly in a body, and so be liable to attack from the hostile Ills, but singly and unobserved, and at infrequent and unexpected intervals.

Hence it is that the earth is full of Ills, for they come and go as they please and are never far away; while Goods, alas! come one by one only, and have to travel all the way from heaven, so that they are very seldom seen.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how did Goods and Ills first affect the concerns of men?
options: Not at all, since men were untouched by either
Only through dreams sent by Jupiter
Equally, so that neither made men altogether blessed or wholly miserable
Only during certain seasons of the year

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what causes the Ills to multiply and grow stronger?
options: The foolishness of mankind
A curse placed by Jupiter
A war among the gods
The disappearance of the Goods

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where do the Goods go to complain about their treatment?
options: To the depths of the sea
To a council of mortal kings
To the underworld
To heaven, to Jupiter

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what do the Goods ask Jupiter to grant them?
options: A permanent home away from mankind entirely
Protection from the Ills and advice on dealing with men
The power to destroy the Ills outright
A new leader to guide them on earth

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does Jupiter decree that the Goods should approach men from now on?
options: Openly and all together, as before
Only through dreams and visions
Singly and unobserved, at infrequent and unexpected intervals
Only once every hundred years

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why is the earth described as full of Ills?
options: Because they come and go as they please and are never far away
Because Jupiter banished the Goods entirely
Because men invited the Ills into their homes
Because the Ills refused Jupiter's protection order

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why are Goods seen so seldom compared to Ills?
options: They are afraid of being seen by mankind
They only appear to those who pray to Jupiter directly
They have been permanently banished from the earth
They come one by one and must travel all the way from heaven

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does Jupiter's decree end up favoring the Ills over the Goods in daily life?
options: Jupiter secretly favors the Ills over the Goods
The Ills, already native to earth, are unaffected by a rule that only limits how the Goods may travel there
The Ills successfully appeal the decree afterward
The Goods refuse to follow Jupiter's new rule

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "intervals" mean in "at infrequent and unexpected intervals"?
options: Places along a journey
Formal agreements between parties
Gaps of time between occurrences
Loud announcements before an event

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the passage?
options: Hardships are common and constant in life, while good fortune arrives rarely and one at a time
Mankind is equally responsible for both good and bad fortune
Jupiter is unfair in how he treats the Goods compared to the Ills
The Ills were created specifically to punish foolish behavior

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Ills seem about to do to the Goods before Jupiter's decree?
options: Destroy them completely so that none remained anywhere
Force them to live permanently among mankind
Trade places with them entirely
Deprive them of all share in human affairs and banish them from the earth

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Goods do in addition to asking for protection?
options: They asked to be allowed to punish the Ills directly
They asked Jupiter's advice on how to deal with men
They asked to remain in heaven permanently
They asked for a new ruler over mankind

questions.prompt: According to the passage, in what way had the Goods previously gone among men, before the new decree?
options: Only in secret, one at a time
Only through dreams
Openly, in a body
Only when specifically summoned

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does Jupiter choose to make the Goods travel singly rather than in a group?
options: To protect them from being overwhelmed by the more numerous and aggressive Ills
To make the Goods harder for mankind to recognize
To punish the Goods for complaining to him
To match how the Ills already traveled among men

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the phrase "in the youth of the world" suggest about when this balance existed?
options: The present day, as things still stand
A brief moment lasting only a single day
A time that exists only in the future
A distant, earlier time before things changed

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "prevail" mean in "the Goods did not prevail to make them altogether blessed"?
options: Speak loudly to be heard
Succeed in achieving an effect
Travel a long distance
Wait patiently for a result

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: Jupiter banishes both Goods and Ills from the earth entirely
The Goods defeat the Ills and take permanent control of human affairs
Jupiter's decree ends up making misfortune common on earth while good fortune stays rare
Mankind asks Jupiter to remove both Goods and Ills from their lives
